items.article: GEN Z are frequently criticised by the older generations for being “lazy” in the workplace. But when it comes to their own businesses,... GEN Z are frequently criticised by the older generations for being “lazy” in the workplace. But when it comes to their own businesses, they are much more motivated than their senior peers. New research suggests 83 per cent of Gen Z entrepreneurs (aged 18 to 28) started their first company before they were 24-years-old. That is compared to eight per cent of Baby Boomers (62-80), nine per cent of Gen X (46-61) and 15 per cent of Millennials (25-40). With youth unemployment at its highest in more than a decade — and roughly one in six 16-24-year-olds without a job — launching a business provides a practical way into work. items.text: Criminal or saviour?Pinto abandoned by Portuguese authorities after City leaks
items.article: Pinto, whose leaks of private documents prompted the investigation into City, has been advised not to return home, contact family members or visit crowded places Man whose leaks of private documents prompted the investigation into City has been advised not to return home, contact family members or visit crowded places M ore than a decade after Rui Pinto set up the Football Leaks website in a crusade triggered by the Fifa scandal in 2015, he finds himself in the middle of a growing storm. The former history student with trademark spiky hair who used to make extra cash selling books about the second world war has not held back with his statements on social media since Manchester City’s guilty verdict from an independent Premier League commission. The first targets for Pinto, whose leaks of private documents prompted first Uefa then the Premier League to investigate City’s financial affairs, were what he alleged were the club’s “cheating” executives for demonstrating “a complete lack of respect for the rules”. On Wednesday he turned his attention to the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino. Less than two hours later, Portuguese authorities confirmed Pinto would no longer be protected as a witness . That is understood to have come as a surprise to the 37-year-old, who finds himself without a job, a home or an income. He has been living in a safe house under protection and has never disclosed his location, and it is understood he has received no visitors. The Guardian understands

items.key: ai:what it was like being in the room for christa pike's botched execution
items.text: What it was like being in the room for Christa Pike's botched execution
items.article: Reporter Will Puckett says he may never sign up to witness another execution after what happened to Christa Pike, but he has no regrets about being there. Puckett, the morning co-anchor for WVLT-TV in Knoxville, Tenn ., was one of seven journalists selected to bear witness to the execution of Christa Pike , who remains alive and in critical condition despite being administered two doses of pentobarbital on Wednesday. "When you agree to be a state-selected witness to an event like this, you know there's the possibility that you'll be called upon to walk people through the events that could be traumatic," Puckett told As It Happens host Nil Köksal. "And that's exactly where we're at today, is just relaying how the state of Tennessee failed to execute Christa Gail Pike appropriately and properly." Pike, 50, was 18 in January 1995 when she, her boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, and a third companion lured their classmate, 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, into a wooded area where they tortured and killed her. Pike and Shipp confessed to the killing and were convicted of first-degree murder. Pike was sentenced to death while Schipp, who was 17 at the time of the crime, was sentenced to life in prison. Years later, Pike expressed remorse for what she'd done. Her lawyers and supporters tried to secure a stay of execution, citing her age at the time of the crime, mental health issues and a history of severe childhood neglect and sexual abuse.

Convicted murderer Christa Pike was due to die by lethal injection at a maximum security prison in Nashville, Tennessee, Wednesday night, only to survive and be raced to hospital . She was in critical condition Thursday and receiving “lifesaving care” at a hospital, her lawyers said. Pike has been on death row for 30 years after she was convicted over the January 1995 killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer . Wednesday night, she was given two doses of pentobarbital , but witnesses described hearing her snoring on the gurney she was strapped to in the chamber. Pike’s attorneys said there were a number of possibilities regarding what went wrong.

items.article: Christa Pike was due to be executed the first woman to be executed in Tennessee for 200 years One of the witnesses who was left horrified watching Christa Pike’s execution attempt has revealed the question the killer asked as things began to go wrong. Pike was due to be executed in Tennessee yesterday (30 September) after the US Supreme Court overturned a last-minute reprieve , clearing the way for her to receive the lethal injection . The 50-year-old, who has spent three decades on death row, was set to be the first-woman put to death in the state for 200 years for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer. However, the execution did not go as planned, and after receiving two syringes of pentobarbital Pike was still ‘alive and snoring’. She was then rushed to hospital where she began receiving ‘life-saving care’. items.key: ai:interpol says ai is increasing speed and scale of cyber threats. here's what companies should watch
items.text: INTERPOL says AI is increasing speed and scale of cyber threats. Here’s what companies should watch
items.article: An INTERPOL executive warns AI is making existing cyber threats faster and harder to detect, while companies face new risks from the rise of agentic AI. Artificial intelligence enables cyber threats by enhancing existing criminal tactics such as scams and fraud, according to INTERPOL. AI is enhancing existing criminal techniques rather than revolutionizing them, Bjorn R. Watne, global chief information security officer at INTERPOL, told CNBC on the sidelines of Tech Week Singapore on Thursday. Scam operators can use AI to target multiple victims simultaneously, while improved translation and digital identities are making it increasingly difficult to distinguish fraudulent interactions from real ones. "It's an evolution and not a revolution," Watne said, adding that AI is primarily increasing the "speed and scale" of existing techniques. As cyber threats evolve, companies should prioritize protective actions, according to Watne. Instead, businesses should first identify their "crown jewels," the assets most critical to keeping their operations running, and determine who would be most interested in stealing or disrupting them. They can then use threat intelligence to understand the tactics and technologies used by those adversaries and tailor their defenses accordingly.

items.key: ai:here's when you actually need to pay tax as a vinted seller (and when you don't)
items.text: Here's When You Actually Need To Pay Tax As A Vinted Seller (And When You Don't)
items.article: Most unwanted item sales are fine, but some cases are worth reporting to HMRC. Second-hand clothing is a serious business. In the UK, resold fashion is estimated to be worth over £7 billion – and it doesn’t seem to be going anywhere. Sites like eBay, Depop, and Vinted are common picks for those looking to buy or sell pre-loved items, from vintage designer jackets to old lamps. But what tax do you need to pay on the income you get from flogging your items? In 2024, the government called out “misinformation... about a new tax for people selling their unwanted clothes or children’s toys, etc. online. This is not right”. All that happened was that they changed how sites like eBay and Vinted have to report sellers’ incomes to HMRC. The reporting changes mean these apps and websites have to let you know that your information has been shared with the tax service if you sell over 30 items or make more than about £1,700 from your sales.

items.key: ai:1 factor may separate women who keep having sex as they age from those who don't
items.text: 1 Factor May Separate Women Who Keep Having Sex As They Age From Those Who Don't
items.article: It doesn’t seem to be due to changed sexual function. There’s no set trajectory for the sex lives of women once they pass 40, according to sexologist Sofie Roos. Some get hornier. Others notice their drive dies down. Hormonal shifts, pain during sex, and life’s many responsibilities all play a role here, the expert previously told us. But a paper published in JAMA Internal Medicine suggests that another factor plays a bigger role in maintaining a sex life as you age than “sexual function”. Among those in midlife or older age, the study found that the “importance” of sex matters. The researchers used data from a group of women who took part in the Do Stage Transitions Result in Detectable Effects (STRIDE) program. This is a cohort study of women who enrolled in 2005, when they were aged between 40 and 65. Starting in year four of the study, participants began answering questionnaires about their sexual function and how important they deemed sex. They also shared information designed to gauge their hormonal state and whether they were sexually active.

items.key: ai:what to know about pike's murder conviction at age 18
items.text: What to know about Pike’s murder conviction at age 18
items.article: Christa Pike, 50, was an accomplice in a murder she committed at 18 of Colleen Slemmer. She was due to be the first woman executed by the state in more than 200 years. Christa Pike, 50, remains in a hospital early Thursday after a botched execution in Tennessee. Pike, the lone woman on death row, was set to be the first female in more than 200 years the state had put to death, according to historical records . However, after she was injected twice with a lethal drug, Pike did not die, and she was transferred to an “off-site medical facility,” a spokesperson for the Department of Correction told NBC News. Attorneys for Pike said late Wednesday that she was being treated at a hospital but that they did not know her condition. In 1995, Knoxville police said Pike and two teenage accomplices had worked together to torture, slash and fatally beat Colleen Slemmer, 19. Police said Pike and the others lured Slemmer, a classmate in their Job Corps training program, to an abandoned steam plant at the nearby University of Tennessee and attacked her. The case became sensationalized when investigators said it was tied to the occult because someone had carved a pentagram into Slemmer’s chest and Pike bragged to another student that she had kept a fragment of the victim’s skull as a “souvenir.”
